items.rule: 42 CFR 2.54 permits de-identified Part2 data disclosed to public health; identifiable SUD patient list still protected absent Part2 consent or another exception.
items.topic: 2026 Part 2 public-health disclosure: de-identified records versus identifiable patient data

option_verdicts.basis: A general HIPAA public-health permission does not bypass Part2 patient-identification rules.
Recipient confidentiality assurances do not substitute for a named patient's Part2 disclosure authority.
HIPAA-standard fully deidentified public-health data may be provided; named record cannot under the given exceptions.
Properly deidentified public-health disclosure is an express Part2 pathway.

items.rule: M.G.L. c94C §21 consumer pamphlet at retail dispensing Schedule II or III, except outpatient palliation, LTCF resident, or treatment of SUD/opioid dependence.
items.topic: Schedule II/III consumer pamphlet: ordinary pain, LTCF, and OUD exceptions

option_verdicts.basis: Ordinary Schedule II postoperative opioid dispensing triggers pamphlet.
LTCF resident is an explicit statutory exemption.
Schedule III buprenorphine patch prescribed for pain still triggers pamphlet.
Buprenorphine/naloxone for OUD falls under the treatment exemption.

items.rule: M.G.L. c112 §12EE(b)-(f): may substitute FDA interchangeable biologic absent written no-substitute; timely prescriber communication, written patient notice and ≥1-year records.
items.topic: Interchangeable biologic substitution: permissive authority, dual notice, and records

option_verdicts.basis: Interchange is permitted rather than mandated just by price, and notices still apply.
No separate prescriber signature is demanded if lawful EHR-alternative notification exists.
Patient notice and durable substitution records cannot be replaced by bare verbal notice and destruction.
Prescriber-accessible pharmacy notation, written patient notice and one-year retention meet described alternatives.

items.rule: Board/DCP Joint Policy 2020-08 (May2023) covers chlamydia EPT, acceptable unnamed EPT profile and required referral if pharmacy unable/unwilling to fill; no gonorrhea coverage by that policy.
items.topic: Chlamydia EPT stock-out referral and disease-specific scope

option_verdicts.basis: Unable-to-fill EPT must be referred, not abandoned.
2020-08 expressly addresses chlamydia, not automatically all STI partners.
Unexamined partner may be represented by 'EPT' and does not need exam/name before referral.
Referral for chlamydia and no reliance on 2020-08 alone for gonorrhea matches scope.

items.rule: Board/DCP Joint Policy 2018-01 II(E), III(A)(i)(d), III(C), IV: earliest CII fill date never changes; DEA may be added; PMP-reportable VI days supply requires consultation; nonreportable VI can change within total quantity.
items.topic: New prescription corrections: earliest-fill dates, DEA number and PMP-sensitive Schedule VI days' supply

option_verdicts.basis: Earliest date on CII is listed as unalterable even after telephone consultation.
A verified omitted DEA number can be added without calling the prescriber.
Gabapentin is a PMP-reportable VI with more restrictive days-supply amendment procedure.
Non-PMP VI amlodipine 30-to-90 day conversion may be pharmacist-driven if quantity total unchanged and documented.

items.rule: 42 USC 300aa-25(b), VAERS provider guidance: manufacturer contraindicating subsequent dose and VAERS-table event within interval are mandatory, mild unlisted soreness and uninjurious error encouraged/not mandatory under NCVIA.
items.topic: VAERS: mandatory adverse-event reports versus encouraged vaccination-error reporting

option_verdicts.basis: Contraindication listed by manufacturer is among mandatory adverse-event reporting types.
Trivial unlisted transient soreness is not by itself in mandatory federal categories.
Table-listed qualifying event is reportable without proved causation.
Vaccination error without adverse event is encouraged for VAERS but not automatically one of the two mandated NCVIA categories.

items.rule: M.G.L. c94C §§19B-19C, Board Policy 2024-01 I-II: third-party naloxone standing order; Schedule II opioid offer; annual Jan15 report if no daily PMP naloxone submission.
items.topic: Naloxone standing order: third-party access, Schedule II offers and reporting alternative

option_verdicts.basis: Standing order permits naloxone kit for someone aiding an at-risk third party.
FDA OTC status does not repeal Massachusetts Schedule II opioid offer duty.
Policy allows standardized 'Naloxone Rescue Kit' profile/label in lieu of purchaser's personal fields for specific standing-order processing.
Instead of daily PMP naloxone uploads, submit annual dose and insurance-dose counts by Jan15.

items.rule: 45 CFR 164.526(b)-(c): amendment ordinarily ≤60 days; one written extension of ≤30 days with reasons and date, successful amendment appended/linked and notified.
items.topic: HIPAA amendment: 60-day response, one extension and linked record correction

option_verdicts.basis: 30-day clock is for HIPAA access rather than the separate 60-day amendment rule.
The pharmacy created the mistaken entry; software vendor does not shift amendment duty.
Oral/two extensions and silent overwrite violate written notice, single extension and documentation.
Written extension before day60, linked accepted amendment, patient and needed recipient notifications satisfy regulation.

items.rule: 247 CMR 16.02(1)(b),(e)-(f),(3): CDTM coverage ≥$1m per occurrence, 5 annual CDTM CE, controlled registration and MassHealth attestation for prescribing, notices of restrictions to every supervising physician.
items.topic: CDTM continuing qualifications: insurance, prescribing registrations, annual CE, and Board restrictions

option_verdicts.basis: Policy limit per occurrence below $1m is insufficient irrespective of annual aggregate.
Five CDTM CE hours recur annually rather than once per two-year contract.
Prescriptive CDTM triggers MCSR, required training and signed MassHealth participation/application attestation.
Board restriction must be disclosed in writing to both supervising physicians even when by consent agreement.

items.rule: USP <797> §14 Category1 and USP FAQ #31/#74: ISO5 PEC in SCA, 12h room BUD or 24h refrigerated, minimum gown/glove requirements same category2.
items.topic: USP <797> Category 1: ISO 5 PEC in an SCA, garbing and short refrigerated BUD

option_verdicts.basis: A Category1 SCA does not permit 24h room-temperature BUD.
With ISO5 PEC, appropriate SCA and full garbing, 24h refrigerated/12h room maximum apply.
Category2 longer BUD requires the qualifying cleanroom suite, not only an upgraded test in unclassified SCA.
Chemical stability at 48h cannot extend Category1 microbiological BUD.

items.rule: 21 CFR 208.24(b)-(e) and 208.26(b): Medication Guides must be supplied on outpatient fills/refills to patient or agent; patient request overrides practitioner direction to withhold.
items.topic: FDA Medication Guides: refill delivery, patient-agent pickup and prescriber no-guide direction

option_verdicts.basis: Manufacturers and dispensers have different Medication Guide responsibilities; pharmacy cannot disclaim delivery.
Agent pickup still receives required Guide on an outpatient refill.
Guide on initial fill does not categorically exempt every refill.
Patient affirmative request triggers Guide even despite prescriber withholding direction.

items.rule: USP <800> §5.1/§10 and USP Jan2026 FAQ 68-71: unpack antineoplastic HD in designated neutral/negative-pressure area, not positive cleanroom; tested chemo glove mandatory; impermeable bag encouraged not universally required.
items.topic: USP <800> receiving: antineoplastic HD unpacking location, chemotherapy gloves and packaging recommendations

option_verdicts.basis: Designated neutral-pressure zone within existing room may be adequate for unpacking; separate room not categorically required.
Positive-pressure ISO7 sterile compounding room is inappropriate for HD shipping carton unpacking.
Use at least one ASTM D6978 chemotherapy glove pair for unpacking Table1 antineoplastics.
Impervious external shipping bag is a recommendation, not universal supplier packaging mandate.

items.rule: FD&C Act 21 USC 351(a)(2)(A),(b) and 352(a): insanitary conditions and substandard strength adulterate; materially false strength label misbrands without injury or recall prerequisite.
items.topic: FD&C Act adulteration versus misbranding: insanitary holding, low potency and false labeling

option_verdicts.basis: Insanitary holding can adulterate absent positive cultured contamination.
Measured materially subpotent lot may be adulterated even if sealed.
Materially false strength is misleading labeling/misbranding independent of patient injury.
Adulterated/misbranded lots are not acceptable for normal dispensing pending a formal FDA recall.

items.rule: 21 CFR 310.501 and 310.515 distinguish mandatory outpatient PPIs for oral contraceptives and specified estrogen products from voluntary patient leaflets.
items.topic: FDA patient package inserts for contraceptives and estrogen products versus voluntary labeling

option_verdicts.basis: Required oral-contraceptive PPI accompanies each outpatient container package.
FDA approval of voluntary patient text does not create universal PPI dispensing mandate.
Estrogen products with PPI duty and hormonal contraceptive products are covered by distinct CFR provisions.
Verbal counseling offer is not an automatic substitute for federally mandated written PPI.

items.topic: PDMA-marked drug samples offered to a pharmacy for repackaging and resale

option_verdicts.basis: Repacks do not evade express pharmacy sample resale/compounding ban.
Reject entire proposed sample stock use for resale or compounding.
Unchanged active drug ingredient does not permit commercial use of sample stock.
Lot/expiry labeling does not convert sample stock into ordinary saleable inventory.

items.rule: 247 CMR 9.18(1)-(5): trained technician may offer counseling; only registered pharmacist or pharmacy intern may deliver medication counseling.
items.topic: Offer to counsel versus actual counseling: trained technician and pharmacy intern

option_verdicts.basis: A technician's right to offer is not authority for clinical dose/missed-dose guidance.
A trained supervised pharmacy intern can counsel, not only a pharmacist.
Licensed pharmacist or intern can answer clinical question while technician limits scope to offer.
A printed leaflet does not nullify accepted counseling obligation.

items.topic: USP <800> risk assessments: intact final dosage form versus manipulated antineoplastic and HD API

option_verdicts.basis: AOR for intact manufactured tablets may justify specified alternative controls if no further manipulation.
Crushing a NIOSH Table1 antineoplastic for compounding disallows replacing required containment with mask alone.
Risk assessments must match product, dosage form and activity, not one blanket for all.
Hazardous bulk API in compounding remains subject to full engineering containment.

items.rule: M.G.L. c94C §21A: patient may decline offered counseling; reasonable effort to document refusal; absent refusal record creates presumption counseling occurred.
items.topic: Patient refusal of counseling and Massachusetts statutory documentation presumption

option_verdicts.basis: The right to decline is explicitly recognized in §21A.
An absence of refusal record creates presumption counseling was PROVIDED, not that it was refused.
Recording declined counseling is the prudent statutory good-faith step.
Offering is distinct from actual accepted counseling; do not falsify the record.

items.rule: 247 CMR 15.02–15.04: prompt patient safety QRE action, report within 24h, ongoing annual personnel training, 2-year records and system analysis.
items.topic: CQI quality-related error: 24-hour documentation versus separate serious-event Board reports

option_verdicts.basis: Immediate patient notification and corrective safety response are duties even absent serious injury.
Initial event documentation cannot be delayed to monthly meeting; 24h clock applies.
QRE records kept ≥2y and CQI education continues annually.
Wrong drug is QRE without requiring injury, hospitalization or death.

items.rule: 105 CMR 722.090(A), 42 CFR 412.92: nonordinary hospital patient inclusion for on-site hospital-owned SNF is conditioned on sole-community-hospital federal qualification.
items.topic: Hospital pharmacy and on-premises hospital-owned skilled nursing residents

option_verdicts.basis: The exemption needs the specified sole-community-hospital criteria in addition to owner/location facts.
An on-campus nursing facility is not automatically hospital inpatient in regulatory definitions.
Off-site ownership alone cannot satisfy the specialized hospital-patient exception.
An eligible properly qualifying hospital SNF may be served, so absolute ban is incorrect.

items.rule: 247 CMR 9.05(1): medical emergency permits less expensive MLID-listed interchangeable product despite no-substitution, with date/time/emergency documented and purchaser written acceptance.
items.topic: Massachusetts emergency interchange despite no-substitution: listed product and written buyer acceptance

option_verdicts.basis: In a qualifying emergency, listed lower-cost interchange can bypass no-substitution instruction.
Alternative must actually be legally interchangeable, not any therapeutically similar product.
Emergency date, time, nature and purchaser's written acceptance are mandatory.
Documenting emergency alone does not waive written acceptance requirement.
